Triage: lands in apps/console MarketplacePage.tsx — pm:queue, domain:ui, type Bug. Rationale: same misdirection class the 5504/5533 lane is already closing (page reports the wrong kind of refusal); the two-line reorder restores the invariant those cards established ("deployment has no marketplace" answers before "who is asking"), so no new decision is needed. Dispatch notes for the ui seat: serial after the 5533 PR lands — the card's own comparison table assumes 5533's detail-page state, and the sibling-page-consistency assertion should be written against the merged ref; the "Not claimed" boundary (admin-first ordering stays correct on marketplace-enabled runtimes) must survive as an explicit test assertion, not just prose. Size/model suggestion: S, sonnet-opus.

**Claim:** `domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_012u2pRjcqAYtoEjgr3wwhnK` · branch `claude/issue-5557-marketplace-runtime-before-admin` · round 4.

## ⛔ Two corrections to the triage note — read before you start

**1. The file is NOT in `apps/console`.** Triage's dispatch note says "lands in apps/console MarketplacePage.tsx". It does not. Measured on `origin/main`:

```
packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/MarketplacePage.tsx
```

There is no marketplace page anywhere under `apps/console/**`. This is a **published library** (`@object-ui/app-shell`), not an app, so the change ships to every workspace consumer — a different risk class from the `apps/console` diff the note anticipated. Re-derive the path yourself rather than trusting either of us.

**2. The serial constraint is already satisfied.** Triage said "serial after the 5533 PR lands". Card #5533 itself returns 404 on read, but its **work is merged** — `.changeset/marketplace-detail-disabled-state-5533.md` and `packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/__tests__/MarketplacePackagePage.disabledState.test.tsx` are both in `origin/main`. So the sibling-consistency assertion can and should be written against the current merged ref. You are not blocked.

## Premise, verified

```
MarketplacePage.tsx:200:  if (!isAdmin) return (MarketplaceAccessDenied);
MarketplacePage.tsx:203:  if (!marketplaceEnabled) return (MarketplaceDisabled);
```

Admin-before-runtime, exactly as claimed. Both components exist as siblings in that directory.

## Scope

`MarketplacePage.tsx`, its test, a changeset. Carry both of triage's requirements as **explicit assertions, not prose**:

- the sibling-page consistency case (catalog and `MarketplacePackagePage` agree for a non-admin on a marketplace-off runtime);
- the **"Not claimed" boundary** — on a marketplace-**enabled** runtime, a non-admin still gets access-denied. That one is the control: without it, a fix that simply deleted the admin check would pass.

Do not touch `MarketplacePackagePage.tsx` — it is the already-fixed sibling and is read-only here.

## ACCEPT — PR #5582

Gates read **by name** on head `880929160`, all 22 runs accounted for:

`Test (shard 1/4)` `(2/4)` `(3/4)` `(4/4)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Doc Component Type Check`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Skill Guide Path Check`, `Live E2E (informational)`, `label` — every one `completed: success`. The three non-success runs are the usual matrix no-ops, all `skipped`. Console performance budget PASS (3784.8 KB against 3867.2 KB).

### What I re-derived rather than relayed

- **The diff is the reorder and nothing else.** Both guards survive; only their order changes, plus comments. No third branch, no altered condition.
- **The boundary control is real.** On a marketplace-**enabled** runtime a non-admin still gets `MarketplaceAccessDenied`, asserted in two cases. This is what stops a "fix" that simply deleted the admin check from passing — the failure mode that would have handed an install surface to every member.
- **`MarketplacePackagePage.tsx` untouched**, as the fence required; it is mounted by the new suite only to compare answers.
- **The new test file is justified, not duplicative.** `MarketplacePage.disabledState.test.tsx` hard-mocks `useIsWorkspaceAdmin: () =. true` at module scope, so no case in it can vary the admin flag. A separate module mock needs a separate file.

### One note on the containment argument — the conclusion holds, the reasoning has a gap

The narrowed vitest run is justified as: *"the changed function body can only execute where the real component is imported"*, with exactly 3 such test files, all inside the directory that was run. I verified the import claim and it is correct — the two other files that mention `MarketplacePage` do so in a **comment** and in a **path-string constant**, not an import.

But that argument does not cover a case this repo actually has: a test that reads the file as **text**. `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/marketplace-preview-namespace-3546.test.tsx` `readFileSync`s `MarketplacePage.tsx` and asserts against its source — in a different package, outside the run.

Harmless here, and I checked rather than assumed: its two assertions over that file are a regex on the `t('marketplace.org.installed', …)` call site and a containment check on the `useObjectTranslation` import line. This diff touches neither, so both are invariant. **But the same argument shape would be wrong on a diff that touched a `t()` call or an import** — worth carrying forward, since source-text gates are invisible to import-graph reasoning.

(My own first pass at checking this said five files imported the component. That was wrong — I had matched the name in comments and a path constant instead of reading the import statements. Corrected before it reached this verdict.)

### The finding filed from a failed test draft: #5583

Worth calling out as method. The first draft of the sibling-consistency case **failed**, and the dev treated the failure as information rather than an obstacle: `MarketplacePackagePage`'s `!isAdmin` guard sits at `:593`, *after* the loading and error branches, so it only refuses once a package resolves.

Verified independently on `origin/main`: guards at `:519` (runtime), `:521` (loading), `:531` (error), `:593` (admin), and the two fetches at `:168`/`:188` are gated on `marketplaceEnabled` but **not** on `isAdmin` — so they do fire on behalf of a viewer the page will refuse. Both of #5583's claims hold. Correctly filed unassigned, correctly declining to decide its own severity.

### Triage's path was wrong; the correction held

Recorded for the triage lane rather than as a complaint: the dispatch note placed this in `apps/console/MarketplacePage.tsx`. Nothing marketplace-related exists under `apps/console/**`; the file is in `packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/`, which makes this a **published library** change rather than an app change. That is the third path error in two rounds (one of them mine), all sharing one cause — `apps/console` and `packages/app-shell/src/console` both read as "the console".

Proceeding to ready-for-review and the merge queue.
